content.text: Inability to maintain pregnancy secondary to premature cervical dilation (esp. in the 2nd TM)
Common cause for recurrent pregnancy loss in the 2nd trimester
May develop pressure, Braxton-Hix-like contractions, bleeding or vaginal discharge esp. in the 2nd TM
PE: painless dilation & effacement of the cervix
Transvaginal U/S: most accurate & predictive to measure cervical length
wide internal os, shortening of the cervical canal, hourglass appearance, bulging of the fetal membrane into the os
insufficiency present if cervical length ≤25mm before 24wks

Cerclage (suturing of cervical os) & bed rest esp. if prior hx – if not performed initially, cerclage can also be performed for women who develop a short cervix (≤25mm) before 24wks as determined by U/S surveillance
May also use weekly injection of 17-alpha-hydroxyprogesterone in addition in some women w/ preterm birth hx
